data.description:
## Context / Problem
In `make verify` on 2026-11-03 PST (worktree fix-caudata, change for `asthmatic-grave-caudata`, based on `0e7401446c5`), xdist worker `gw1` died while running `tests/unit/test_opcert_key_copy_leak_tortoise.py::test_signer_test_modules_leave_no_key_copy_in_the_temp_dir`. The crash guard printed `xdist worker=gw1 terminated abnormally: Not properly terminated`, and pytest reported the test FAILED with no traceback.

Observations:
- The whole run took 4 h 51 min wall. The usual time is 25 to 30 min. Afterwards, host load average was about 35 and free memory about 9%.
- Run alone afterwards, the same test passed (26 passed with 3 other modules, 4 min 05 s).
- The test starts a nested pytest (`tests/_nested_pytest.py::run_nested_pytest`) over the signer modules. `deformed-cherubical-flycatcher` (closed) previously covered that nested run exceeding its time budget.

Hypotheses (unproven): host memory pressure killed the worker; the nested run hit an internal bound and the worker exited without reporting; something else.

## Approach
Reproduce under controlled load: run the module under `pytest -n 4` while a bounded memory-pressure helper runs. Record the worker exit signal (macOS jetsam log via `log show --predicate "eventMessage CONTAINS \"jetsam\""`) and peak RSS of the nested run. Fix the class once the cause is confirmed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The cause of the gw1 death is identified with recorded evidence (exit signal or log line) in a comment on this ticket.
- [ ] A fix or an explicit no-defect finding is recorded, with the test passing under `make test` on the reproducing host.
data.title: xdist worker dies in opcert key-copy tortoise test during a slow, loaded make verify
